rules.law_name: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.title: Annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent only once within the annual cap: no more than 3% of current rent or 80% of the CPI change, whichever is less. The page also states the ordinance allows, but does not require, a registration pass-through fee, and a landlord charging more than $50 must reimburse the tenant for the overpayment.
rules.key_value: 3% or 80% of CPI change, whichever is less; current maximum 2.87% for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027; pass-through fee capped at $50
rules.penalty: If a landlord charges a tenant a pass-through fee greater than $50, the landlord shall reimburse the tenant for the registration fee pass-through overpayment.
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord can only raise your rent by a certain amount each year. The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.law_name: Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.title: Just cause eviction protections
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, a lease violation, or owner move-in. For certain evictions, the landlord may have to provide relocation assistance for moving costs.
rules.key_value: Valid reason required; relocation assistance for certain evictions
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
